newsitem.title: POLAND: OLAWA TEMPORARILY GIVES UP NEW SHARE ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: OLAWA TEMPORARILY GIVES UP NEW SHARE ISSUE.

text.p: Polish non-ferrous metals smelter Olawa SA temporarily gave up a new share issue of up to 1,350,000 shares, concerned that its shareholders would refuse to accept it, the deputy president of the company said.

Andrzej Latka told Reuters that the management of the firm would ask the general shareholders meeting, postponed until December or January, to consider a share issue or other forms of acquiring capital, but no decisions were expected.

"The new share issue will not be voted on the nearest general shareholeders meeting but we will ask our shareholders whether we should find funds we need through a share issue or other forms such as bank loans," he said.

He said the funds from the new issue, estimated at about 20 million zlotys, were intended mostly for investment in two of its main suppliers Zaklady Gorniczo-Hutnicze Boleslaw and Huta Cynku Miasteczko Slaskie.

"We wanted to create a raw material base for ourselves and later take about 25-percent stakes in the firms," he said adding that uncertainty over Boleslaw's privatisation might cause shareholders' unwillingness to carry out a new issue.

Olawa's main shareholders are the state treasury, holding a 16.7-percent stake, Polish mutual trust fund Pioneer - 10.4 percent, Irena 10 percent, bank Pekao SA 7.7 percent and Bank Gdanski 5.0 percent.
